probe.title: Reversing a trip cash receipt after its trip settled credits CASH_VAN again: van cash goes negative and office CASH stays overstated
probe.role: Accountant (money desk; owner and manager take the same MONEY_DESK route POST /receipts/{id}/reverse)
probe.platform: API (core spec on a test database)
probe.environment: Worktree .claude/worktrees/b2-suspects, branch qa/b2-suspects at bcc7fda (the tip of main; git merge --ff-only main said "Already up to date"). Postgres 17 on 127.0.0.1:5439, database dos_test_b2_sus (a copy of dos_test_batch2b_template, migrated). Node 24, vitest 4.1.11, DATABASE_POOL_MAX=3. The spec harness src/testing/app.ts booted DeliveryModule, WarehouseModule, BillingModule, OrdersModule, InventoryModule, ReceivablesModule, FilesModule and SyncModule, so the trip-settled predicate from DeliveryModule.onModuleInit was registered, as it is on the real services.
steps: 1. Fixture: a fresh tenant with bootstrapTenant, one shop, one variant at Rs 10 a piece with 12% GST, and 1000 pieces of opening stock at the godown.
2. Salesperson: POST /orders with 1 case, then POST /orders/{id}/submit. Warehouse: POST /warehouse/orders/{id}/pack. This issued INV/0001 for 13400 paise.

3. Owner: POST /delivery/vehicles. Driver: POST /delivery/consents. Warehouse: POST /delivery/trips with one stop carrying INV/0001 and openingCashPaise 0, then POST /delivery/trips/{id}/start-loading. Driver: POST /delivery/trips/{id}/depart. The trip is now active.
4. Driver: POST /delivery/stops/{id}/start, POST /delivery/stops/{id}/arrive, and POST /delivery/deliveries (full delivery, signature as proof of delivery).
5. Driver: POST /delivery/collections with mode cash and 13400 paise. This created RCPT-0001 with Dr CASH_VAN 13400 / Cr AR 13400.

6. Driver: POST /delivery/trips/{id}/return, so the trip is closing. Accountant: GET /delivery/trips/{id}/settlement read expected cash 13400. Accountant: POST /delivery/trips/{id}/settle with handedOverCashPaise 13400. Trip state became settled with no variance.

7. Accountant: GET /receipts/{id} returned status collected, depositedAt null, withCrew false (the cash is in the office). Balances were read by SQL (sum of journal_lines per account) and by GET /receivables/accounts.
8. Accountant: POST /receipts/{id}/reverse with reversalId and reason 'entered against the wrong shop'.
9. Read the receipt_reversal journal lines and the CASH, CASH_VAN and AR balances again, by SQL and by GET /receivables/accounts.
probe.expected: The settlement already moved the trip's cash from CASH_VAN to CASH (Dr CASH 13400 / Cr CASH_VAN 13400). The reversal should take the money out of CASH, where it now is: Dr AR 13400 / Cr CASH 13400. Afterwards CASH_VAN should be 0, CASH should be 0 and AR 13400, and the trial balance should show no negative cash with the crews.
probe.actual: Book after collection: CASH_VAN 13400, CASH 0, AR 0. Settlement lines: CASH +13400, CASH_VAN -13400. Book after settle, by SQL and by GET /receivables/accounts: CASH 13400, CASH_VAN 0, AR 0. The reverse call returned 200 and created RCPT-0002 (cash, -13400, status cancelled); the original RCPT-0001 is now cancelled. Reversal lines: AR +13400, CASH_VAN -13400, and no CASH line. Book after undo, identical by SQL and by the desk's GET /receivables/accounts: AR 13400, CASH 13400, CASH_VAN -13400. The undo changed CASH_VAN by -13400 and CASH by 0. A second run on a new tenant (s75a-22028645) gave the same rows and balances as the first (s75a-21993993).
probe.businessImpact: Undoing a doorstep cash receipt after Day-end is routine: a receipt entered against the wrong shop, or cash handed back. Each time, the accountant's trial balance shows negative cash with the delivery crews (-Rs 134 here, which is physically impossible) and office cash Rs 134 higher than what is in the till or was refunded. At the next cash count the desk looks short by the reversed amount, and the accountant takes the blame. If the desk then records the corrected receipt at the office, CASH is debited again and the overstatement stays. Total cash (CASH + CASH_VAN) and AR are right, so no money is lost or paid twice. But the split between office cash and crew cash is wrong in an append-only journal, and it can only be fixed with a manual correcting entry. That is a major operational issue for the Day-end reconciliation, not a total-ledger corruption, hence P1.

probe.rootCause: backend/libs/core/src/modules/receivables/receivables.service.ts:1921-1923 in undoReceipt picks the source account as `original.depositedAt ? 'BANK' : receiptAccountCode(original.mode, original.tripId)`. receiptAccountCode (:280-283) returns 'CASH_VAN' for any cash receipt with a tripId, and undoReceipt never checks whether that trip has settled. The service already has that check: `this.tripSettled`, registered by DeliveryModule.onModuleInit (delivery/delivery.module.ts:79) and used by getReceipt at :791 and depositReceipts at :902-907. The settlement already posted Cr CASH_VAN for the trip's cash (delivery/settlement.service.ts:235-239), so the reversal credits CASH_VAN a second time. depositReceipts has the same situation and handles it correctly by passing a null tripId (:928-930, the DOS-132 fix); undoReceipt was not updated in that fix (git blame: lines 1920-1924 are unchanged since 8ea449a1, 2026-09-05).
probe.suggestedFix: In undoReceipt, before building the lines, check the trip when the receipt is not deposited, has a tripId and is cash. Run the same predicate getReceipt uses (`select (${this.tripSettled(sql`${original.tripId}`, tenantId)}) as settled`) inside the same transaction. If the trip has settled, use receiptAccountCode(mode, null), which gives CASH; otherwise keep CASH_VAN. Keep the depositedAt → BANK branch first. To stop a reversal racing a settlement on the same trip, take the trip-settled read under the lock settle takes (read the trip row FOR SHARE, or through a delivery-supplied locking predicate) so the account choice and the settlement's Cr CASH_VAN cannot disagree. No contract or schema change is needed.

probe.title: Two simultaneous POST /receipts/deposit calls for the same receipt both return 200: the receipt is banked twice, BANK doubles and CASH/CHEQUES go negative
probe.role: Money desk: Accountant and Manager (the Owner can also bank)
probe.platform: API (core spec on a test database: HTTP through Fastify inject into ReceivablesModule, real TenantGuard, permission matrix and DbModule)
probe.environment: Worktree qa/b2-suspects at c679499 (= main, 'git merge --ff-only main' printed 'Already up to date.'). Libraries already built. Postgres 17 on 127.0.0.1:5439, database dos_test_b2_sus (a copy of dos_test_batch2b_template with 48 of 48 migrations applied), default_transaction_isolation = read committed. Node 24, vitest 4.1.11, DATABASE_POOL_MAX=3. Probe tenants: s75b-5ce32634 (run 1) and s75b-118938be (run 2), both removed afterwards by recreating the database from the template.
steps: 1. As the accountant, record an office receipt of Rs 100 (10 000 paise): POST /receipts with mode cash (or cheque with reference and bankName), no trip. Reply is 200, status 'collected', tripId null.

2. At the same moment, send two requests: the accountant sends POST /receipts/deposit {id: batchA, idempotencyKey: dep-s75b-batchA, receiptIds: [receipt], depositRef: DEP-A-n} and the manager sends the same with batchB, its own key and DEP-B-n (Promise.all of two app.inject calls with pre-signed desk tokens).
3. Read the receipt row (status, deposit_ref), the deposit journal_entries for batchA and batchB with their journal_lines by account code, and the ChequeDeposited outbox_events for the receipt.
4. Run A: repeat steps 1-3 thirty times, alternating cash and cheque.

5. Run B: repeat five more times while a third connection holds 'select ... for update' on the receipt row for 1.5 s. Both desk requests then pass their status check before either writes; count the backends waiting on a lock in pg_stat_activity, then release.
6. Run C (control): bank the same receipt twice one after the other, accountant then manager.
7. Read the probe tenant's totals: receipts by mode, account balances for BANK/CASH/CHEQUES/AR, deposit entries, unbalanced entries.
probe.expected: For each concurrent pair, exactly one call answers 200 and the other 409 'receipt ... is deposited, not collected'. The receipt carries exactly one deposit journal entry (BANK +10 000, CASH or CHEQUES -10 000) and one ChequeDeposited event. Tenant totals: BANK equals the Rs 3 600 actually collected, and CASH and CHEQUES are 0.
probe.actual:
Run 2 (per-run log in probe-log.txt):
- Run A: 30 of 30 pairs both 200 (each 'updated=1,total=10000'). Every receipt shows receipt.status=deposited, depositEntries=2, BANK=20000, CASH or CHEQUES=-20000 and ChequeDepositedEvents=2. deposit_ref is whichever desk wrote last (DEP-B-n in 26 runs, DEP-A-n in 4).
- Run B: 5 of 5 pairs both 200. pg_stat_activity showed backendsWaitingOnLock=2, both inside 'update "receipts" set "status" = ...', so both had already passed the status check.
- Run C (sequential): first 200, second '409(receipt RCPT-0036 is deposited, not collected)'.
- Tenant totals after run 2: 36 receipts, Rs 3 600 collected (cash 210 000 + cheque 150 000 paise). 71 deposit journal entries. BANK +710 000 (Rs 7 100), CASH -200 000, CHEQUES -150 000, AR -360 000, 0 unbalanced entries.
- SQL for RCPT-0001 and RCPT-0002: each has two deposit entries, DEP-A-n posted_by the accountant (...73c1) and DEP-B-n posted_by the manager (...73c0), each BANK +10000 / CASH or CHEQUES -10000, and two ChequeDeposited events.

Run 1 (database only; vitest hid the console lines): 34 of 35 concurrent pairs doubled. 70 deposit entries for 36 receipts, BANK +700 000 against 360 000 collected, CASH -190 000, CHEQUES -150 000.

Overall, 69 of 70 concurrent pairs banked the same receipt twice. Each sequential control banked once.
probe.businessImpact: A shop pays Rs 100 in cash. The manager presses 'Bank this batch' on Day-end while the accountant presses 'Bank it' on the receipt panel (the owner's Money > Receipts screen can bank too). Both screens say it worked. The books now show Rs 200 in the bank and Rs -100 cash in hand for Rs 100 of real money. The bank statement will never reconcile, cash in hand and cheques in hand go negative, and BANK is overstated in every balance and report built from the journal. One deposit call accepts up to 200 receipts, so a single clash on a full Day-end batch doubles the whole day's banking (for example Rs 2 lakh shows as Rs 4 lakh). For a cheque, a later bounce reverses only one of the two deposits, so BANK stays overstated. The journal is append-only, so the fix is a manual reversing entry, and nothing tells anyone it happened. ChequeDeposited fires twice, so anything that consumes it acts twice. The receipt's deposit_ref and deposited_at are silently overwritten by the second desk, so the receipt points at a different batch than the first journal entry. This is financial corruption in normal two-desk use, hence P0 by the charter; the row's P1 was a pre-verification guess.

probe.rootCause:
backend/libs/core/src/modules/receivables/receivables.service.ts, depositReceipts (line 870):
- :876-879 reads the batch's receipts with a plain SELECT, without FOR UPDATE, inside withTenant's READ COMMITTED transaction.
- :883-888 checks status 'collected' against that unlocked snapshot, so a second desk whose read happens before the first desk commits also sees 'collected'.
- :933-942 updates receipts filtering only on tenant_id and id. There is no status = 'collected' condition and the updated row count is never checked. When the first transaction commits, the second one's UPDATE (which was waiting on the row lock) re-checks its WHERE clause, still matches, and overwrites status, deposit_ref and deposited_at.
- :943-956 posts the journal with idempotencyKey `journal:deposit:${input.id}`. That key is unique per batch id, so a second batch posts a second Dr BANK / Cr CASH or CHEQUES entry.
- :957-963 emits ChequeDeposited again.
- The only serialisation point, idempotent() in backend/libs/core/src/platform/idempotency.ts:57-61, applies to requests that reuse the same key, not to two desks with different keys.
probe.suggestedFix: In depositReceipts, lock the batch before checking it. Change the select at receivables.service.ts:876-879 to `...where(...).orderBy(receipts.id).for('update')`. The ordering stops two overlapping batches from deadlocking. The second desk then waits for the first to commit, reads the committed status 'deposited', and gets the existing 409. As a second guard, add `eq(receipts.status, 'collected')` to the UPDATE's WHERE at :942 with `.returning({ id: receipts.id })`, and throw ORPCError CONFLICT (which rolls back the journal and events) when the returned count is not input.receiptIds.length. No schema or contract change is needed. The same read-then-update pattern is worth checking in undoReceipt (reverse and bounce) as a separate item.

skeptic.reason:
Upheld: I could not refute it. When two desks bank the same collected receipt at the same moment, both calls succeed. Each call posts its own Dr BANK / Cr CASH or CHEQUES entry and emits its own ChequeDeposited event.

The probe takes the same path as the app:
- Same endpoint: POST /receipts/deposit, the call made by the manager app's Day-end (day-end.tsx:135), its Money panel (money/index.tsx:156) and the owner app's Money > Receipts (owner-app receipts.tsx:85).
- Same roles: MONEY_DESK at permissions.ts:604 admits owner, manager and accountant.
- Same body: id, idempotencyKey, receiptIds, depositedAt, depositRef.
- Same keys: each device's useMutation builds its own id and key (api-client client.ts:90-91), so two desks always send different keys.
- Deposit has no offline-sync handler (receivables.sync.ts has none), so this online call is the only path.

Nothing else in the product prevents the outcome. Queried on dos_test_b2_sus:
- Triggers on receipts: only receipts_tombstone and receipts_touch_updated_at.
- The receipts_write_update policy checks only the tenant and a non-retailer role.
- journal_entries has only UNIQUE(tenant_id, idempotency_key). The deposit key is `journal:deposit:${batchId}`, so each batch is unique and nothing ties a receipt to a single deposit.
- ChequeDeposited is listed as AUDIT_ONLY at backend/worker/src/jobs/outbox-coverage.test.ts:40, so no job reconciles afterwards.
- The server has no FOR UPDATE and no status guard (receivables.service.ts:876-879 and :933-942, as the prober cited).

Reproduction:
- Prober's spec re-run: 34 of 35 concurrent pairs banked twice.
- My probe through the real manager and owner services: 18 of 20 simultaneous pairs banked twice.
- On a bounce after a double deposit, the cheque's net is still BANK +10000 and CHEQUES -10000.
- The owner's GET /receivables/accounts shows the inflated BANK.

probe.businessImpact:
Vans often lose signal, and the delivery app's own offline path records a doorstep payment as a 'receipts' op. The Day-end cockpit does not see any of that cash.
- Honest crew: each offline cash receipt over Rs 100 shows as cash over. The accountant or manager cannot close the trip, it goes to the owner's approval queue, and it closes red (settled_with_variance). When the owner accepts, the shop's payment is booked as a made-up cash-over gain (CASH_SHORT, overstating income), and the same amount stays in CASH_VAN for good (overstating van cash). Every offline receipt makes the books worse.
- Dishonest or careless crew: they hand over only the float and keep the offline cash. The settlement is green, variance 0, no approval. Meanwhile the shop's bill shows paid and the accountant's cash-in-hand list says the money is in the office. At Rs 672 a bill, a driver with 10 offline cash stops could keep Rs 6,720 in one day with nothing flagged.
This is money going missing and the ledger being wrong in normal daily work, so it meets the charter's P0 'financial corruption'. That is above the P1 in the suspect row, because trip 2 shows theft goes unnoticed.
The only repair is an API call no screen offers (manager, before settlement, knowing the receipt id), and the accountant role gets 404 on it.

When it comes back, the godown cannot load it again from W7: it drops out of 'Packed orders' for good, even though the planning board still offers it. The re-attempt goes out with no manager load-out approval, no blind package count and no challan line. It leaves only because trips.depart dispatches it without saying so. The van's paperwork then understates the load. In the run, the challan and sheet declared ₹134 and ewbRequired=false while ₹268 of bills were on the van, which equals the e-way bill threshold. A real re-delivery that pushes a load to or past the ₹1 lakh default would leave without the e-way bill number being asked for, which risks the vehicle being detained and a GST penalty.
